flags.detail: Paraphrasing-tool ('tortured phrase') language: 32 corrections were needed (29 in the abstract and 3 in the body). Examples: 'posture a multifaceted ... challenge in present day medication' (pose ... present-day medicine), 'These complexes disarrange display a interesting set of impediments in both clinical hone and inquire about' (These complex disorders present a unique set of challenges in both clinical practice and research), 'hazard components' (risk factors), 'conclusion and administration' (diagnosis and management), 'maniacal clutters' (psychotic disorders), 'enthusiastic' (emotional), 'hereditary, natural ... variables' (genetic, environmental ... factors), 'improvement and movement of these disarranges' (development and progression of these disorders), 'exact recognizable proof' (accurate identification), 'pharmacological intercessions' (interventions), 'way of life alterations' (lifestyle modifications), 'brain-degenerating diseases' (neurodegenerative diseases), 'brain flexibility' (neuroplasticity), 'looking at body signs' (biomarker analysis). The abstract is the second Introduction paragraph ('It presents a diverse array of difficulties ... vast spectrum of neuropsychiatric disorders') sentence for sentence, run through a synonym-substitution tool. This is a typical way of hiding copied or AI-generated text from similarity checkers. All corrections are listed in 'changes'. Before publication: run a similarity check (iThenticate/Turnitin) on the original manuscript, ask the author to write a new abstract in their own words, and get a signed originality declaration.

AI-generated or 'AI-humaniser' text with an editor's/assistant's instruction left in. The sections from Literature Review to Results, plus Final Research Result, Findings of the Study, Conclusion paragraphs 2-6 and Suggestions, are in a different, simplified register ('brain problems', 'talk therapy', 'how good life feels'). Key words are systematically deleted ('The study of disorders', 'show up in ways', 'have causes', 'In cases', 'In term or worsening illnesses', 'important for conditions'), which is the signature of an automated 'humaniser' tool. The Methodological limitations paragraph ended with an instruction to the author: 'If the paper is meant to be a review the methods should be updated with real search dates, search words, inclusion rules and screening steps.' It was removed. The same template sections (Research Gap, Research Questions, Hypotheses, Scope/Significance/Relevance, International Perspective) also appear in the case-pendency paper, so they may have been added by whoever prepared the manuscripts, not by the author. Words were restored only where the meaning was unambiguous (see 'changes'). These vague phrases are still in the text, worded as in the source, for the author to complete: Findings 'Importance of recognition', 'Clinical value of tools', 'Need for treatment' (the item says no single treatment suits every disorder), 'Value of care', 'Stigma, constraints', 'individuals experiencing injury'; Suggestions 'Promote screening', 'Improve capacity', 'Encourage treatment'; Objective 5 'the importance of healthcare'; H₁/H₀ 'psychological and environmental dimensions'; 'help in understanding disorders'; 'Studies on care that includes areas of health'; 'how to diagnose health issues'; 'The study also matters for health' (twice); 'people working in sciences'; 'just having advances'; 'help study problems'; 'combinations of susceptibility'; 'development of interventions'; 'health awareness'; 'selection of methods'. Ask the author to confirm these sections, fill in the missing words, and sign an AI-use declaration (COPE position on AI tools).

Figure 1 and the Introduction's opening sentences appear to be taken from Miyoshi & Morimura, 'Clinical Manifestations of Neuropsychiatric Disorders', Chapter 1 (pp. 1-14) of reference 1 (Miyoshi, Morimura & Maeda, Neuropsychiatric Disorders, Springer, 2010). That chapter's abstract recommends calling psychiatric symptoms or syndromes caused by organic cerebral disorders 'neuropsychiatric symptoms' or 'neuropsychiatric syndromes', and the three-domain diagram (neuropsychiatric / neuropsychological / neurological symptoms) appears to reproduce its figure. The manuscript's caption gives no source and there is no permission statement. No source line was added, because that would be added content. Before publication: the author should confirm the source and either obtain permission from Springer Nature or replace the figure with an original one. The caption should then read 'Adapted from Miyoshi and Morimura (2010)^1^'. The redrawn PNG keeps the labels exactly as in the manuscript ('Delusion', 'etc', 'Motor & Sensory Functions Reflexes, Etc').

The .docx file was created on 11 April 2024 by 'shri hari computers' (a typing/DTP service), has 27 revisions and was last modified by 'DR RAVI TYAGI' on 18 October 2026. The core text appears to date from that 2024 version: the abstract, Introduction, Types / Causes / Diagnostic / Treatment sections, the first Conclusion paragraph and the reference list (latest reference 2022). The research-style sections appear to be later additions. A 2024 manuscript may already have been submitted to, or published in, another journal, conference volume or edited book between 2024 and 2026. A web search for the exact title and distinctive phrases found no earlier publication, but this is not conclusive because many regional journals are not indexed. Before publication: get a signed declaration from the author that the work is original, unpublished and not under consideration elsewhere, and run a similarity check.

Reference 25 (reference 26 in the manuscript), 'Javed, A., & GetUsers, P. (2019). Genetics of neuropsychiatric disorders. Advances in Experimental Medicine and Biology, 1192, 589-601', looks corrupted or fabricated. 'GetUsers, P.' is not a plausible personal name (it looks like a software artefact), and a web search could not confirm such a chapter. The author must verify it, or replace it with a real source that supports the 'Implementing genetic testing' section. It is kept as given.

Other reference problems (all kept as given). (a) Ref 22 (Gorelick, 'Role of inflammation in cognitive impairment: results of observational epidemiological studies and clinical trials'): as far as I can tell (not confirmed online), this paper was published in Ann N Y Acad Sci 2010;1207:155-162, not '2019, 1443(1), 19-33'. Check the year, volume and pages. Ref 22 has no numeric citation in the text (cited only as 'Gorelick (2019)' in the Literature Review). (b) 'Vascular factors' cites ^21^ (Najjar 2013, neuroinflammation; [22] in the manuscript), the same source as 'Neuroinflammation'. [23] in the manuscript was probably intended, but Gorelick is about inflammation, so no cited source supports the vascular-factors paragraph. (c) Sources that do not match the claims: Malaspina 2001 (paternal age and schizophrenia, ref 13) is cited for schizoaffective disorder; Lefaucheur 2017 (tDCS guidelines, ref 29) for TMS and DBS; Ramos & Arnsten 2007 (adrenergic pharmacology and cognition, ref 11) for GABA/noradrenergic imbalance in anxiety. (d) Ref 1 is cited as a whole book but ends '1, 1-14' (the chapter pages). It should be cited as the chapter (Miyoshi & Morimura, Clinical manifestations of neuropsychiatric disorders, pp. 1-14). (e) Refs 29 and 30 shorten their author lists without an ellipsis. Refs 6 and 7 (web pages) have no access dates. (f) The Literature Review uses author-year citations while the rest of the paper uses numbers. The International Perspective, Research Gap, Scope/Significance/Relevance, Results and Findings sections (WHO and DSM claims included) have no citations. (g) Manuscript refs 8 and 13 were identical (DSM-5, 2013) and have been merged, so manuscript refs 14-32 are now numbered 13-31.

This is a narrative review (published as a Review Article) but uses research-article sections. Research Methodology reports no actual search: no dates, no databases actually searched (it says they 'can be used'), no search terms, no inclusion/exclusion counts. It states Hypotheses, including a null hypothesis (H₀), that are 'not statistically tested'; the third is labelled only 'Hypothesis:' (probably H₂). 'Results' comes before the review content (Types, Causes, Diagnostic Approaches, Treatment), and 'Results', 'Final Research Result' and 'Findings of the Study' repeat each other. The first Conclusion paragraph (2024 text) overlaps paragraphs 2-6, and its last sentence is ungrammatical ('it is crucial in enhancing the well-being of those impacted ...'; left unchanged). Kept as submitted, per the light-edit policy. Recommended restructure for the author: Introduction → Methods (search strategy) → thematic sections (Types, Causes, Diagnosis, Treatment) → Discussion (merge Results, Final Research Result, Findings) → Conclusion → Suggestions. Drop H₀/H₁ or recast them as review questions.

Anxiety disorders are listed under Mood disorders but treated as a separate category in the Scope. Some Figure 1 labels could be tidied with the author's consent ('Delusion' → 'Delusions'; 'Motor & Sensory Functions Reflexes, Etc' → 'Motor and sensory functions, reflexes, etc.').
